content: The page lists three possible choices of relations defining an atelier structure on the family F. The first pair, ≤ and ≪, is enclosed; the second uses ≤ and the curved subdivision-order sign; the third uses ≪ and the compatibility glyph.
It recalls an earlier choice of ≤ and the subdivision sign, defines ≪ as their generated preorder, and writes G ≪ F iff there exists F′ with G ≤ F′ followed by the subdivision relation to F.

The lower paragraph associates the earlier choice with the geometric and intuitive priority of subdivision over refinement. It calls the derivation of transitivity and, literally, reflexivity laborious and says this led to surplus axioms. It tentatively prefers starting from ≤ and ≪ and calls the compatibility-based alternative a curiosity.
The upper margin rejects sufficiency under a new point of view. The slanted note refers forward to manuscript page 20 and says the subdivision relation will instead be determined from ≪ and ≤.
math_reading_decisions: The two F primes in (1.29) are read individually as small high-right strokes; ordinary G and F operands remain distinct from the footed family F in the opening.
The order sign has a curved lower rule and is rendered preccurlyeq. Both compatibility occurrences have free diagonal ends and no horizontal caps; the upper occurrence has visible reinforcement.
The heavy double chevron in the verbal definition is live retracing, with no independent cancellation line identified.
The factorization formula and generated-preorder assertion were read, not proved. The page’s relation to any earlier axiom system was not investigated.
The S row is confirmed only as to literal reflexivity and the inserted surtout. Its proposed antisymmetry correction remains unverified and is not incorporated.
